solutions.check: 27 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Stuffy First Lady gutted, hosting worst balls-up

indicators.note: a balls-up is a mess or botch, so the letters are jumbled out of order
a host takes guests in, so one piece sits inside the other
a gutted fish has its insides removed, so only the outer shell of the phrase survives

parts.note: the two words treated as one run, keeping only the outside letters
the five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A dowdy First Lady makes a dreadful mess of her duties as hostess.
explanation.walkthrough: F and Y wrap round the jumbled ROWST to make FROWSTY; 'balls-up' is British slang for a botched job.
explanation.definitionFit: Frowsty is a British word for a room that is close, musty and badly ventilated.

clue.text: Bird of prey hit balls after erection

parts.note: to rap is to strike sharply

indicators.note: in a down clue, erecting something stands it upright so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: balls is slang for nonsense, as is rot

explanation.surface: A lewd scene: someone strikes a man's testicles once he is aroused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Balls' means nonsense here, not anatomy, and 'erection' is not sexual: in a down clue, raising a word up makes it read bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A raptor is any hunting bird such as a hawk, eagle or falcon that seizes prey with talons.

clue.text: Hoy down cycling with PM? That's the spirit!

indicators.note: cycling sends the letters round and round until they settle in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; PM is also Prime Minister

explanation.surface: Sir Chris Hoy, the British Olympic track cyclist, takes a spin with the Prime Minister, and someone cheers him on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' fits Hoy so neatly that it reads as the sport, not the signal; the exclamation 'That's the spirit!' hides the definition at its end.
explanation.definitionFit: A wood nymph is a dryad, a female nature spirit of classical myth living in trees.

clue.text: Chuck's worth screwing

indicators.note: screwing twists something round, so the letters are twisted into a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A crude remark that a man called Chuck would be a good bedfellow.
explanation.walkthrough: Chuck looks like a man's name, but it is the verb; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To chuck something is informally to toss or hurl it, a casual synonym.

clue.text: A load of pisspoor, insecure right-wingers entering the fracas

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: a fracas is a noisy brawl

indicators.note: a wing on the right side of a word is its final letter, so only the closing letters are kept

parts.note: the final letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A gang of incompetent, nervous right-wing politicians joins a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right-wingers' looks like a description of Tories; it means the right-hand letters of the two preceding words, which slip into FIGHT after the F.
explanation.definitionFit: Freight is goods carried in bulk by lorry, ship or train, which is to say a cargo.

clue.text: "Don't accept Biden!" Donald eventually starts to go? Nothing of worth in that

parts.note: to refuse is to decline to accept

indicators.note: letters told to go must leave, so they are struck out

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only first letters are taken

parts.note: the opening letter of each word

explanation.surface: Trump urges supporters to reject Biden's victory, and the writer adds that the whole affair is worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts to go' looks like Biden beginning to leave office; it is the first letters of the two names being removed. The definition is a whimsical description.
explanation.definitionFit: A refuse bin is a container for rubbish, and rubbish is by nature stuff without value.

clue.text: Deli trashed by Republican time-waster

indicators.note: something trashed is wrecked, so the letters are smashed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
R is the standard abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A delicatessen is vandalised by a Republican layabout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' here means placed beside, so R simply follows the rearranged deli.
explanation.definitionFit: An idler is a lazy person who fritters hours away doing nothing useful.

clue.text: Suspend Brenda, in regard to being a parasite

parts.note: to suspend something is to hang it
Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the late Queen, Elizabeth Regina, whose cipher is ER
on means concerning, as in a book on birds

explanation.surface: A call to suspend a woman called Brenda for sponging off others.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye has long called Queen Elizabeth II 'Brenda', so this is a satirical swipe at royal freeloading; ER is her royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanger-on is a sycophantic follower who lives off someone richer, a social parasite.

clue.text: Under the influence of drugs, cry mayhem

parts.note: being up means high on stimulants
to roar is to cry out loudly

explanation.surface: Someone high on drugs bellows for chaos, like a warrior crying havoc.
explanation.walkthrough: The long opening phrase is not the definition but just two letters: 'up' as in high, slang for being on uppers.
explanation.definitionFit: An uproar is a noisy public commotion, so it matches the chaos and turmoil of mayhem.

clue.text: Bond's after hit item of male jewellery

indicators.note: coming after means following in sequence, so one piece is set behind the other

parts.note: to cuff is to strike with an open hand
a link is a bond or connection

explanation.surface: James Bond is going after a hit-man, or perhaps a hit record, wearing a gentleman's accessory.
explanation.walkthrough: Bond invites thoughts of 007, who suits the accessory, but it is just a link; 'Bond's after' means bond is after.
explanation.definitionFit: A cufflink fastens a shirt cuff and is one of the few pieces of jewellery men conventionally wear.

clue.text: Conservative working with Middle Eastern rulers ropes in Tory leader — they're doing well out of Brexit and Coronavirus

definitions.text: they're doing well out of Brexit and Coronavirus

parts.note: Con is the abbreviation for a Conservative

indicators.note: roping something in draws it inside a circle, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: sultans are Muslim sovereigns, notably in the Middle East

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Tory in league with Gulf rulers draws in the party chief, and the clue sneers at those profiting from Brexit and Covid.
explanation.walkthrough: T goes inside SULTANS before the last S. The definition is a satirical description: the government paid private consultancy firms huge sums during Brexit and the pandemic.
explanation.definitionFit: Management consultants were hired at great cost by the British government for Brexit planning and Covid testing, so they profited from both.

clue.text: see 22ac.
Flatulence protection a motorist needs to face up to?

definitions.text: a motorist needs to face up to?
definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the thing, not a synonym

parts.note: wind is gas in the gut
a screen shields or protects

explanation.surface: A comic image of a driver needing a shield against a passenger's farts.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'face up to': a driver literally faces the glass in front, rather than confronting a problem. 'Windscreen' is the British word for windshield.
explanation.definitionFit: A windscreen is the glass panel at the front of a car that the driver looks straight through.

clue.text: Trump, having lost power, obtains a potty for self-gratification

indicators.note: potty means crazy, so the letters are thrown into a mad new order
something lost is gone, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: taken as written
P is the physics symbol for power
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Trump, ousted from office, takes a toilet for his own pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potty' looks like a noun, a child's toilet, but it is the adjective meaning crazy: TRUM with OBTAINS and A is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Masturbation is sexual stimulation of oneself, quite literally pleasuring the self.

clue.text: Bloomer made by tabloid, loud and inferior

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
F is forte, the musical direction for loud
lower means of lesser rank or quality

explanation.surface: A blunder committed by a brash, low-grade tabloid newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a howler, the kind a tabloid makes, but it means something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunflower is a tall plant with big yellow flowers, so it is something that blooms.

clue.text: Method of arranging cheque in post at last

indicators.note: arranging puts things into a new order, so the letters are laid out afresh

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, so only that one is taken

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A tip on how to pay: put the cheque in the post at the last moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At last' reads as 'finally, after delay' but takes only the end letter of post.
explanation.definitionFit: A technique is a particular way of doing something, which is what a method is.

clue.text: Andrew, possibly one with 'mature' marital relationship

parts.note: Andrew Marr is a well-known British political journalist and TV presenter
I is the Roman numeral one
to mature is to age

explanation.surface: A sly dig at Prince Andrew, perhaps a man with an older partner.
explanation.walkthrough: Andrew suggests the prince, but the 'possibly' signals another Andrew: Marr, the BBC interviewer.
explanation.definitionFit: Marriage is the legally or formally recognised union of spouses, which is a marital bond.

clue.text: President on record (perversely) "I WANNA STAY HERE"

definitions.note: a cryptic description of the place, voiced by its reluctant occupant

parts.note: George Washington was the first US president

indicators.note: doing something perversely means doing it the wrong way round

parts.note: a CD, compact disc, is a record

explanation.surface: A president is heard on tape insisting, perversely, that he refuses to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: Written as Trump stood refusing to concede defeat in 2020: the 'here' he wants to stay in is the US capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The White House sits in the US capital, so a president clinging on to office wants to remain in that city.

clue.text: Split second to stuff Chip

indicators.note: stuffing pushes filling inside something, so one piece is packed within another

parts.note: a chip is a small bit broken off
sec is the short form of second, as in 'wait a sec'

explanation.surface: A split second is all it takes to stuff a man named Chip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split second' reads as one phrase, but split is the definition and second the filling.
explanation.definitionFit: To bisect is to cut into two equal parts, which is a precise way to split.

clue.text: Trump-style sullen aggression? 'Crazy uncle' to rest in peace

indicators.note: resting in a place means lying inside it
something crazy is all over the place, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the five letters rearranged
a truce is a peace agreement

explanation.surface: Trump's surly belligerence likened to a mad uncle who should be laid to rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rest in peace' looks like a burial phrase but splits: the jumbled uncle goes inside TRUCE. Trump's niece Mary wrote of her 'crazy uncle'.
explanation.definitionFit: Truculence is an eagerness to fight or argue, a surly and defiant hostility.

clue.text: Star judge abandons party

indicators.note: to abandon is to leave, so those letters walk out of the word

parts.note: to party is to celebrate
to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: A celebrity talent-show judge quits a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' is a verb here, and 'judge' a verb too: RATE leaves CELEBRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Celeb is informal shorthand for a celebrity, a famous person or star.

clue.text: 'Boot out old Trump finally!' The Mexican

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter is used

parts.note: the final letter of the word
el is Spanish for 'the'

explanation.surface: A Mexican demands that Trump, now old news, be thrown out at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Mexican' means the Spanish word for 'the', and 'finally' takes only the last letter of Trump, not the end of his term.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel is to force someone out, a formal synonym of the slang phrase.

clue.text: (& 11ac.) Precisely identify part of member that may grow long and blue

parts.words: part of member that may grow long
parts.note: a fingernail is part of a limb, or member, and grows if left uncut
feeling blue is feeling low or depressed, in a slump

explanation.surface: A smutty hint at a male member that grows long and turns blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' means a limb, a finger or toe here; the double-entendre is the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail something down is to establish or pin it down exactly, an idiom for fixing facts.

clue.text: Actor Doris associated with Hamilton?

parts.note: Doris Day was a Hollywood singer and actress
Lewis Hamilton is the British Formula One champion

explanation.surface: A question whether some actor is linked with the musical Hamilton.
explanation.walkthrough: Each name is completed by its partner: Doris's surname and Hamilton's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Day-Lewis is a British-Irish film star with three Best Actor Oscars.

clue.text: Orgasmed noisily — pissed off

indicators.note: something done noisily is heard, so the sound matters more than the spelling

parts.note: to reach a climax is to peak

explanation.surface: Someone climaxed loudly and then felt irritated.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb to peak and the adjective for annoyed are pronounced alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Piqued means irritated or resentful after a slight, which is the slang sense of annoyed.

clue.text: Be worn out with northern babe

indicators.note: out means awry or disordered, so the letters are knocked out of place

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: Feeling exhausted alongside a northern girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worn out' reads as a single idiom for tired, but out is the signal and N joins the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A babe in the old sense is an infant, and a newborn is a baby just delivered.

clue.text: Donald entertained to some extent (not too hard)

indicators.note: to some extent means partly, so only a portion of the words is used

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Trump was mildly amused, but in a restrained way.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket looks like an aside qualifying the entertainment but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Al dente is Italian for pasta cooked firm to the bite, so still slightly hard, but not too hard.
